variants.title: Cs-137 with a CsI(Tl) scintillator
variants.unknown: the energy resolution of CsI(Tl) at 662 keV
variants.note: CsI(Tl) is denser than NaI(Tl) and brighter, but its light is red and matches a photomultiplier less well.

source.title: G. F. Knoll, Radiation Detection and Measurement, 4th ed.: typical energy resolution at 662 keV of scintillation detectors

variants.title: Cs-137 with a BGO scintillator
variants.unknown: the energy resolution of BGO at 662 keV
variants.note: BGO stops gamma rays best of the three (high Z, density 7.13 g/cm3) but yields a third as much light as NaI(Tl).

source.title: G. F. Knoll, Radiation Detection and Measurement, 4th ed.: typical energy resolution at 662 keV of scintillation detectors

variants.title: Cs-137 with a plastic scintillator: the Compton edge
variants.unknown: the Compton edge energy of the 662 keV line
variants.note: Plastic is hydrogen and carbon: no photopeak, only the Compton continuum, which ends at the Compton edge.

source.title: G. F. Knoll, Radiation Detection and Measurement, 4th ed., ch. 2: Compton edge T_max = E 2a/(1+2a), a = E / 511 keV
